from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import sqlite3
import threading
from contextlib import contextmanager
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Callable, Iterator

from .model import epoch_millis

# One truncation event, as handed to :meth:`Store.insert_truncation`.
TruncationRecord = tuple[str, str, str, int, int, int]

ACTION_VERSION_APPENDED = "version_appended"
ACTION_WINDOW_TRUNCATED = "window_truncated"


class Store:
    """Append-only persistence for entity versions.

    Rows in ``versions`` are never deleted.  A correction appends its own row
    and closes the ``valid_end`` of the value it supersedes; every closing is
    also appended to ``truncations``, which records *when the system learned*
    the bound, so a transaction-time reader can tell a declared bound from one a
    later correction pulled back.
    """

    def __init__(self, path: str, clock: Callable[[], datetime] | None = None):
        if path != ":memory:":
            Path(path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.clock = clock or (lambda: datetime.now(timezone.utc))
        # One connection is shared across request threads, so every use of it is
        # serialised by this lock.  A write holds it across its whole
        # transaction, which is what commits different batches one after another
        # (continuous versions, non-overlapping windows) and stops any reader on
        # another thread observing a half-applied batch.  It is reentrant so the
        # read helpers a write calls while holding the lock can take it again.
        self.lock = threading.RLock()
        self.connection = sqlite3.connect(path, isolation_level=None, check_same_thread=False)
        self.connection.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        self.connection.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL")
        self.connection.executescript(
            """
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS entities (
              type TEXT NOT NULL,
              id TEXT NOT NULL,
              created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
              PRIMARY KEY (type, id)
            );
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS versions (
              type TEXT NOT NULL,
              id TEXT NOT NULL,
              attribute TEXT NOT NULL,
              version INTEGER NOT NULL,
              operation TEXT NOT NULL,
              value TEXT,
              valid_from INTEGER NOT NULL,
              valid_end INTEGER,
              declared_end INTEGER,
              recorded_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
              PRIMARY KEY (type, id, attribute, version)
            );
            CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS versions_by_attribute
              ON versions(type, id, attribute, valid_from);
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS truncations (
              type TEXT NOT NULL,
              id TEXT NOT NULL,
              attribute TEXT NOT NULL,
              version INTEGER NOT NULL,
              recorded_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
              valid_end INTEGER NOT NULL
            );
            CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS truncations_by_version
              ON truncations(type, id, attribute, version, recorded_at);
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS idempotency (
              key TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
              operation TEXT NOT NULL,
              response TEXT NOT NULL
            );
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS audit_events (
              seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
              event_id TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
              recorded_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
              action TEXT NOT NULL,
              type TEXT NOT NULL,
              id TEXT NOT NULL,
              attribute TEXT NOT NULL,
              version INTEGER NOT NULL,
              operation TEXT,
              value TEXT,
              valid_from INTEGER,
              declared_end INTEGER,
              valid_end INTEGER
            );
            CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS audit_events_scan
              ON audit_events(recorded_at, event_id);
            """
        )
        self._backfill_audit()

    @staticmethod
    def audit_event_id(*parts: Any) -> str:
        """Deterministic, collision-resistant identity for one audit item.

        The digest is taken over the immutable ledger coordinates of the event
        — its action, entity coordinates, version, transaction instant, and the
        payload the write committed — so the same committed row always derives
        the same id, while two distinct events cannot share one.  A version
        later corrected carries different coordinates and therefore a different
        id, so an old audit item can never be retroactively rewritten.
        """
        joined = "\x1f".join("" if part is None else str(part) for part in parts)
        return hashlib.sha256(joined.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()

    def _backfill_audit(self) -> None:
        """Project rows written by older releases into the audit ledger.

        Databases created before the audit entry point existed hold committed
        ``versions`` and ``truncations`` rows but no audit items.  Every such
        row is described once here, in the same deterministic order fresh
        writes use: transaction time first, then stable entity and version
        coordinates.

        Each projection runs in one transaction, so a crash can never leave it
        half applied; the UNIQUE index on ``event_id`` makes a re-run idempotent
        as well, so reopening a database can never double-fill it.
        """
        with self.lock:
            already = self.connection.execute(
                "SELECT 1 FROM audit_events WHERE action = ? LIMIT 1",
                (ACTION_VERSION_APPENDED,),
            ).fetchone()
            if already is None:
                version_rows = self.connection.execute(
                    """
                    SELECT type, id, attribute, version, operation, value,
                           valid_from, declared_end, recorded_at
                      FROM versions
                     ORDER BY recorded_at, type, id, attribute, version
                    """
                ).fetchall()
                legacy: list[tuple[Any, ...]] = []
                for row in version_rows:
                    event_id = self.audit_event_id(
                        ACTION_VERSION_APPENDED,
                        row["type"], row["id"], row["attribute"], row["version"],
                        row["recorded_at"], row["operation"], row["value"],
                        row["valid_from"], row["declared_end"],
                    )
                    legacy.append(
                        (
                            event_id,
                            int(row["recorded_at"]),
                            ACTION_VERSION_APPENDED,
                            row["type"], row["id"], row["attribute"], int(row["version"]),
                            row["operation"], row["value"],
                            int(row["valid_from"]), row["declared_end"], None,
                        )
                    )
                if legacy:
                    self.connection.execute("BEGIN")
                    try:
                        self.connection.executemany(
                            """
                            INSERT OR IGNORE INTO audit_events(
                                event_id, recorded_at, action, type, id, attribute, version,
                                operation, value, valid_from, declared_end, valid_end)
                            VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
                            """,
                            legacy,
                        )
                    except Exception:
                        self.connection.execute("ROLLBACK")
                        raise
                    else:
                        self.connection.execute("COMMIT")
            already = self.connection.execute(
                "SELECT 1 FROM audit_events WHERE action = ? LIMIT 1",
                (ACTION_WINDOW_TRUNCATED,),
            ).fetchone()
            if already is None:
                truncation_rows = self.connection.execute(
                    """
                    SELECT rowid, type, id, attribute, version, recorded_at, valid_end
                      FROM truncations
                     ORDER BY recorded_at, type, id, attribute, version, valid_end, rowid
                    """
                ).fetchall()
                legacy = []
                for row in truncation_rows:
                    event_id = self.audit_event_id(
                        ACTION_WINDOW_TRUNCATED,
                        row["type"], row["id"], row["attribute"], row["version"],
                        row["recorded_at"], row["valid_end"], row["rowid"],
                    )
                    legacy.append(
                        (
                            event_id,
                            int(row["recorded_at"]),
                            ACTION_WINDOW_TRUNCATED,
                            row["type"], row["id"], row["attribute"], int(row["version"]),
                            None, None, None, None, int(row["valid_end"]),
                        )
                    )
                if legacy:
                    self.connection.execute("BEGIN")
                    try:
                        self.connection.executemany(
                            """
                            INSERT OR IGNORE INTO audit_events(
                                event_id, recorded_at, action, type, id, attribute, version,
                                operation, value, valid_from, declared_end, valid_end)
                            VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
                            """,
                            legacy,
                        )
                    except Exception:
                        self.connection.execute("ROLLBACK")
                        raise
                    else:
                        self.connection.execute("COMMIT")

    @contextmanager
    def transaction(self) -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:
        # Serialise whole transactions: BEGIN IMMEDIATE takes the write lock at
        # once, and the RLock keeps every other thread (readers included) off the
        # shared connection until COMMIT, so a batch is atomic to the outside.
        with self.lock:
            self.connection.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
            try:
                yield self.connection
            except Exception:
                self.connection.execute("ROLLBACK")
                raise
            else:
                self.connection.execute("COMMIT")

    def now(self) -> int:
        """Current instant as integer milliseconds since the Unix epoch."""
        return epoch_millis(self.clock().astimezone(timezone.utc))

    @staticmethod
    def encode(value: Any) -> str:
        return json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True)

    @staticmethod
    def decode(value: str) -> Any:
        return json.loads(value)

    # -- entity bookkeeping -------------------------------------------------

    def entity_row(self, entity_type: str, entity_id: str) -> sqlite3.Row | None:
        with self.lock:
            return self.connection.execute(
                "SELECT created_at FROM entities WHERE type = ? AND id = ?",
                (entity_type, entity_id),
            ).fetchone()

    def insert_entity(self, entity_type: str, entity_id: str, created_at: int) -> None:
        self.connection.execute(
            "INSERT INTO entities(type, id, created_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
            (entity_type, entity_id, created_at),
        )

    def entity_keys(
        self, entity_type: str | None = None, entity_id: str | None = None
    ) -> list[tuple[str, str, int]]:
        """Every entity in scope, with its record instant, in stable order.

        A ``type`` alone selects every entity of that type, a ``type``/``id``
        pair one entity, and no argument the whole store.  Rows come back
        ordered by the stable identifier ``(type, id)``, so a caller walking
        the result always visits entities in the same sequence.
        """
        clauses = []
        parameters = []
        if entity_type is not None:
            clauses.append("type = ?")
            parameters.append(entity_type)
        if entity_id is not None:
            clauses.append("id = ?")
            parameters.append(entity_id)
        where = "" if not clauses else " WHERE " + " AND ".join(clauses)
        with self.lock:
            rows = self.connection.execute(
                f"SELECT type, id, created_at FROM entities{where} ORDER BY type, id",
                parameters,
            ).fetchall()
        return [(str(row["type"]), str(row["id"]), int(row["created_at"])) for row in rows]

    # -- versions -----------------------------------------------------------

    def versions_for_entity(self, entity_type: str, entity_id: str) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:
        with self.lock:
            return list(
                self.connection.execute(
                    """
                    SELECT attribute, version, operation, value, valid_from, valid_end,
                           declared_end, recorded_at
                      FROM versions
                     WHERE type = ? AND id = ?
                     ORDER BY attribute, valid_from, version
                    """,
                    (entity_type, entity_id),
                ).fetchall()
            )

    def versions_for_attribute(
        self, entity_type: str, entity_id: str, attribute: str
    ) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:
        with self.lock:
            return list(
                self.connection.execute(
                    """
                    SELECT attribute, version, operation, value, valid_from, valid_end,
                           declared_end, recorded_at
                      FROM versions
                     WHERE type = ? AND id = ? AND attribute = ?
                     ORDER BY valid_from, version
                    """,
                    (entity_type, entity_id, attribute),
                ).fetchall()
            )

    def next_version(self, entity_type: str, entity_id: str, attribute: str) -> int:
        with self.lock:
            row = self.connection.execute(
                """
                SELECT COALESCE(MAX(version), 0) + 1 AS next
                  FROM versions
                 WHERE type = ? AND id = ? AND attribute = ?
                """,
                (entity_type, entity_id, attribute),
            ).fetchone()
        return int(row["next"])

    # -- truncations --------------------------------------------------------

    def truncations_for_entity(self, entity_type: str, entity_id: str) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:
        with self.lock:
            return list(
                self.connection.execute(
                    """
                    SELECT attribute, version, valid_end, recorded_at
                      FROM truncations
                     WHERE type = ? AND id = ?
                     ORDER BY recorded_at, attribute, version
                    """,
                    (entity_type, entity_id),
                ).fetchall()
            )

    def truncate_attribute(
        self,
        entity_type: str,
        entity_id: str,
        attribute: str,
        at: int,
        effective: int,
        recorded_at: int,
    ) -> list[TruncationRecord]:
        """Apply a correction landing at ``at`` that takes effect at ``effective``.

        The version straddling ``at`` keeps its value and only has its
        ``valid_end`` pulled back to ``at``; ``declared_end`` keeps the bound the
        assertion itself declared, so a reader before this write can still see
        the window as it stood when the row was written.

        Every version that starts at or after ``at`` is superseded: it holds no
        valid time from ``at`` onwards.  Its own declared ``valid_end`` stays
        where it was, because a bounded assertion keeps its own bound; the
        truncation records the instant the new value took the window over.

        ``effective`` differs from ``at`` only for a backdated correction with an
        explicit ``valid_from``: the correction is placed in the past but takes
        effect at the instant the version it supersedes did, which is what lets a
        restated past win from ``valid_from`` onwards while the value it
        displaced collapses.

        Every window that this correction closes gets a row in ``truncations``,
        stamped with ``recorded_at`` — the transaction instant the bound was
        learned at, never a business instant.  A truncation is knowledge, so it
        must be datable on the axis a reader filters on: a reader whose
        ``known_at`` is earlier than this write must not see the end it pulled
        back.  Recording one row per event, rather than one stamp per version, is
        what keeps that exact when a later correction pulls the same window back
        twice.

        Only versions recorded no later than this request are touched, so the
        versions inserted by the correction that calls this method cannot
        supersede one another, while a previous correction recorded at the same
        millisecond is still superseded correctly.
        """
        rows = self.connection.execute(
            """
            SELECT version, valid_from, valid_end, declared_end
              FROM versions
             WHERE type = ? AND id = ? AND attribute = ? AND recorded_at <= ?
            """,
            (entity_type, entity_id, attribute, recorded_at),
        ).fetchall()
        events: list[TruncationRecord] = []
        for row in rows:
            version = int(row["version"])
            if int(row["valid_from"]) >= at:
                # A version starting at or after the landing point holds no valid
                # time from there on: it is superseded, not trimmed.
                events.append(
                    (entity_type, entity_id, attribute, version, recorded_at, effective)
                )
                continue
            end = None if row["valid_end"] is None else int(row["valid_end"])
            if end is not None and end <= at:
                # A bound the version declared itself already stops before the
                # landing point, so the correction takes no valid time from it.
                continue
            declared = None if row["declared_end"] is None else int(row["declared_end"])
            self.connection.execute(
                """
                UPDATE versions
                   SET valid_end = ?, declared_end = ?
                 WHERE type = ? AND id = ? AND attribute = ? AND version = ?
                """,
                (
                    at,
                    declared,
                    entity_type,
                    entity_id,
                    attribute,
                    version,
                ),
            )
            events.append(
                (entity_type, entity_id, attribute, version, recorded_at, at)
            )
        if events:
            # Insert one row at a time so the stable rowid of each truncation is
            # known: a version can be superseded more than once inside one
            # batch, which yields truncation rows identical on every column, and
            # only their persistent rowids tell those distinct events apart.
            audit_rows: list[tuple[Any, ...]] = []
            for event in events:
                cursor = self.connection.execute(
                    """
                    INSERT INTO truncations(type, id, attribute, version, recorded_at, valid_end)
                    VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
                    """,
                    event,
                )
                audit_rows.append(
                    (
                        self.audit_event_id(
                            ACTION_WINDOW_TRUNCATED,
                            event[0], event[1], event[2], event[3], event[4], event[5],
                            cursor.lastrowid,
                        ),
                        event[4],
                        ACTION_WINDOW_TRUNCATED,
                        event[0], event[1], event[2], event[3], event[5],
                    )
                )
            self.connection.executemany(
                """
                INSERT INTO audit_events(
                    event_id, recorded_at, action, type, id, attribute, version,
                    operation, value, valid_from, declared_end, valid_end)
                VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, ?)
                """,
                audit_rows,
            )
        return events

    def insert_version(
        self,
        entity_type: str,
        entity_id: str,
        attribute: str,
        version: int,
        operation: str,
        value: Any,
        valid_from: int,
        valid_end: int | None,
        recorded_at: int,
    ) -> None:
        encoded = None if value is None else self.encode(value)
        self.connection.execute(
            """
            INSERT INTO versions(type, id, attribute, version, operation, value,
                                 valid_from, valid_end, declared_end, recorded_at)
            VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
            """,
            (
                entity_type,
                entity_id,
                attribute,
                version,
                operation,
                encoded,
                valid_from,
                valid_end,
                valid_end,
                recorded_at,
            ),
        )
        event_id = self.audit_event_id(
            ACTION_VERSION_APPENDED,
            entity_type, entity_id, attribute, version, recorded_at,
            operation, encoded, valid_from, valid_end,
        )
        self.connection.execute(
            """
            INSERT INTO audit_events(
                event_id, recorded_at, action, type, id, attribute, version,
                operation, value, valid_from, declared_end, valid_end)
            VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, NULL)
            """,
            (
                event_id,
                recorded_at,
                ACTION_VERSION_APPENDED,
                entity_type,
                entity_id,
                attribute,
                version,
                operation,
                encoded,
                valid_from,
                valid_end,
            ),
        )

    # -- idempotency --------------------------------------------------------

    def idempotent_response(self, key: str, operation: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
        row = self.connection.execute(
            "SELECT operation, response FROM idempotency WHERE key = ?", (key,)
        ).fetchone()
        if row is None or row["operation"] != operation:
            return None
        return self.decode(row["response"])

    def remembered_operation(self, key: str) -> str | None:
        row = self.connection.execute(
            "SELECT operation FROM idempotency WHERE key = ?", (key,)
        ).fetchone()
        return None if row is None else str(row["operation"])

    def remember(self, key: str, operation: str, response: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        self.connection.execute(
            "INSERT INTO idempotency(key, operation, response) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
            (key, operation, self.encode(response)),
        )

    # -- audit --------------------------------------------------------------

    def max_audit_seq(self) -> int:
        """The sequence assigned so far; the upper bound a first page pins."""
        with self.lock:
            row = self.connection.execute("SELECT COALESCE(MAX(seq), 0) AS m FROM audit_events").fetchone()
        return int(row["m"])

    def audit_key_exists(self, recorded_at: int, event_id: str, upper_seq: int) -> bool:
        """Whether a cursor's last-returned item is a real row in this store.

        The ledger is append-only, so a cursor this store issued always finds
        its position here.  A token minted against another database (or one
        pointing past the pinned result set) does not, which is how such a
        cursor is reported as unknown instead of silently walking foreign
        data.
        """
        with self.lock:
            row = self.connection.execute(
                "SELECT 1 FROM audit_events WHERE recorded_at = ? AND event_id = ? AND seq <= ?",
                (recorded_at, event_id, upper_seq),
            ).fetchone()
        return row is not None

    def audit_page(
        self,
        *,
        after_recorded_at: int | None,
        after_event_id: str | None,
        upper_seq: int,
        limit: int,
        action: str | None = None,
        entity_type: str | None = None,
        entity_id: str | None = None,
        attribute: str | None = None,
        recorded_from: int | None = None,
        recorded_to: int | None = None,
    ) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:
        """One stable page of audit items.

        Ordering is ``(recorded_at, event_id)`` ascending: ``recorded_at``
        puts the items on the transaction axis, and the event id breaks ties
        inside one millisecond.  Event ids derive from the immutable
        coordinates of the committed event, so that tie-break is stable, never
        reused, and identical after a restart — the order lives in the rows,
        not in a clock reading.

        Pagination is keyset-based: the cursor carries the last seen
        ``(recorded_at, event_id)`` pair, which is what makes pages overlap-
        and gap-free even when several events share a millisecond.
        ``upper_seq`` independently pins the result set: items committed
        after the first page was opened (their ``seq`` is higher) never
        enter later pages, so a concurrent writer cannot move the window
        the cursor walks.
        """
        clauses = ["seq <= ?"]
        parameters: list[Any] = [upper_seq]
        if after_recorded_at is None:
            # Nothing has been consumed yet: the lower recorded-time bound, if
            # any, is the only starting line.
            if recorded_from is not None:
                clauses.append("recorded_at >= ?")
                parameters.append(recorded_from)
        else:
            # Strictly after the last returned key, on the same ordered pair.
            clauses.append("(recorded_at > ? OR (recorded_at = ? AND event_id > ?))")
            parameters.extend([after_recorded_at, after_recorded_at, after_event_id])
            if recorded_from is not None:
                clauses.append("recorded_at >= ?")
                parameters.append(recorded_from)
        if action is not None:
            clauses.append("action = ?")
            parameters.append(action)
        if entity_type is not None:
            clauses.append("type = ?")
            parameters.append(entity_type)
        if entity_id is not None:
            clauses.append("id = ?")
            parameters.append(entity_id)
        if attribute is not None:
            clauses.append("attribute = ?")
            parameters.append(attribute)
        if recorded_to is not None:
            clauses.append("recorded_at < ?")
            parameters.append(recorded_to)
        sql = (
            "SELECT seq, event_id, recorded_at, action, type, id, attribute, version, "
            "operation, value, valid_from, declared_end, valid_end FROM audit_events"
            " WHERE "
            + " AND ".join(clauses)
            + " ORDER BY recorded_at, event_id LIMIT ?"
        )
        parameters.append(limit + 1)
        with self.lock:
            return list(self.connection.execute(sql, parameters).fetchall())

296	def known_windows(versions: list[Version], known_at: int) -> list[Token]:
297	    """Reconstruct the valid windows of one attribute as known at ``known_at``.
298	
299	    Every version is known from its ``recorded_at`` onwards, and every truncation
300	    it carries from the ``recorded_at`` of that truncation onwards.  Working from
301	    the newest version the reader can see back to the oldest, a version holds
302	    valid time from its own ``valid_from`` until the earliest of:
303	
304	    * ``valid_from`` of the next version the reader can see, because the value
305	      written later is the one in force from then on;
306	    * the end it carries for that reader, which is its declared ``valid_end`` or,
307	      while the trim that pulled the end back is still unknown, nothing at all;
308	    * the instant a correction already known at ``known_at`` starts writing
309	      there, which is where the chain of visible corrections takes over.
310	
311	    A version whose only displacers are recorded after ``known_at`` keeps an open
312	    ended window, because at that instant nobody had written the bound — that
313	    rule is what keeps a transaction-time view exact.  Tokens come back in
314	    transaction order, oldest first.  Retraction rows always carry an empty
315	    window: they exist to mark the instant an attribute ceased to exist.
316	    """
317	    ordered = sorted(versions, key=lambda item: (item.valid_from, item.version))
318	    tokens: list[Token] = []
319	    takeover: int | None = None
320	    for index in range(len(ordered) - 1, -1, -1):
321	        version = ordered[index]
322	        if version.recorded_at > known_at:
323	            # Not recorded yet for this reader, and it could not have displaced
324	            # anything either: it is invisible to the whole pass.
325	            continue
326	        following = next(
327	            (
328	                ordered[other]
329	                for other in range(index + 1, len(ordered))
330	                if ordered[other].recorded_at <= known_at
331	            ),
332	            None,
333	        )
334	        if version.operation == "retract":
335	            # A retraction never holds valid time of its own; it only closes the
336	            # window in front of it.
337	            end: int | None = version.valid_from
338	        else:
339	            end = version.end_known_at(known_at)
340	            if following is not None:
341	                # A version the reader can see takes over where it begins.
342	                end = following.valid_from if end is None else min(end, following.valid_from)
343	            if takeover is not None:
344	                # A correction already known at ``known_at`` starts writing at
345	                # that instant, which is the end of everything before it.
346	                end = takeover if end is None else min(end, takeover)
347	        tokens.append((version, version.valid_from, end))
348	        takeover = version.valid_from
349	    tokens.sort(key=lambda token: (token[0].recorded_at, token[0].version))
350	    return tokens

353	def complete_windows(versions: list[Version], known_at: int) -> list[Token]:
354	    """The windows as they stand in the ledger, for a history listing.
355	
356	    Every version the reader can see keeps the end the ledger records for it,
357	    with any trim the reader cannot know about yet left out, so this is the
358	    full-knowledge view of the ledger for that transaction instant rather than a
359	    projection: a window a correction pulled back shows the pulled back end once
360	    that correction is knowable, and a value displaced by a backdated
361	    restatement keeps the part of its own window that no later version took over.
362	    """
363	    ordered = sorted(versions, key=lambda item: (item.valid_from, item.version))
364	    tokens: list[Token] = []
365	    for index, version in enumerate(ordered):
366	        if version.recorded_at > known_at:
367	            # Recorded after the reader's instant, so this reader never saw it.
368	            continue
369	        end = version.end_known_at(known_at)
370	        successor = next(
371	            (
372	                ordered[other]
373	                for other in range(index + 1, len(ordered))
374	                if ordered[other].recorded_at <= known_at
375	            ),
376	            None,
377	        )
378	        if successor is not None:
379	            end = successor.valid_from if end is None else min(end, successor.valid_from)
380	        tokens.append((version, version.valid_from, end))
381	    tokens.sort(key=lambda token: (token[0].valid_from, token[0].version))
382	    return tokens

385	def project(tokens: list[Token], at: int) -> Token | None:
386	    """Select the value that was in force at business instant ``at``.
387	
388	    Tokens arrive in transaction order, newest first.  A backdated correction can
389	    leave two windows that touch: the value it displaced keeps the window it had,
390	    and the restated value covers the earlier part of it.  The value written last
391	    is the one the ledger believes from the instant it took effect, so the
392	    newest match wins.
393	    """
394	    for token in reversed(tokens):
395	        start, end = token[1], token[2]
396	        if start <= at and (end is None or at < end):
397	            return token
398	    return None

401	def _projection_content_same(first: Projection, second: Projection) -> bool:
402	    """Whether two projections carry the same public data content.
403	
404	    What counts is what a read reports as data: every attribute's value and
405	    the valid window it holds.  The version number that supplies the value
406	    and the transaction instant the row was recorded at are storage
407	    bookkeeping, so they may differ freely without making the records differ.
408	    """
409	    if set(first) != set(second):
410	        return False
411	    for name in first:
412	        left, right = first[name], second[name]
413	        if not value_same(left[0], right[0]):
414	            return False
415	        if (left[2], left[3], left[4]) != (right[2], right[3], right[4]):
416	            return False
417	    return True

522	    effect, each attribute's business value, and the full public version

525	    an interval split, or a retraction therefore registers as a change
526	    whenever it moves what either side ultimately observes, even when the
527	    business value happens to be the same; intermediate versions that neither
528	    viewpoint sees never enter the comparison.

530	    if set(first) != set(second):

534	        # Values go through the store's own equality so a boolean and a number
535	        # stay distinct (Python itself would equate ``true`` and ``1``); the
536	        # remaining tuple fields are exactly the public version metadata.
537	        if not value_same(left[0], right[0]):
538	            return False
539	        if left[1:] != right[1:]:
540	            return False

580	    def run_batch(self, raw: Any, key: str | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
581	        """Atomically apply an ordered list of creates and corrections.
582	
583	        Every item shares one transaction instant, so the whole batch is one
584	        point on the transaction axis: later items see earlier items' effects,
585	        but no outside reader ever sees a partially applied batch.  Any invalid
586	        or conflicting item aborts the transaction and nothing is stored.
587	        """
588	        moment = self.store.now()

590	        # Entities this very batch will create, so a correction whose creation
591	        # sits later in the array can be told apart from one that names an
592	        # entity nobody will ever create: the first is an ordering conflict,
593	        # the second is simply not found.
594	        created_here = {
595	            (item.entity_type, item.entity_id)
596	            for item in operations
597	            if isinstance(item, BatchCreate)
598	        }
599	
600	        def action(recorded_at: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
601	            results: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
602	            seen_creates: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
603	            for index, item in enumerate(operations, start=1):
604	                target = (item.entity_type, item.entity_id)
605	                try:
606	                    if isinstance(item, BatchCreate):
607	                        start = item.valid_from if item.valid_from is not None else recorded_at
608	                        document = self._create_core(
609	                            item.entity_type,
610	                            item.entity_id,
611	                            item.attributes,
612	                            start,
613	                            recorded_at,
614	                        )
615	                        seen_creates.add(target)
616	                        document["operation"] = "create"
617	                    elif isinstance(item, BatchCorrect):
618	                        try:
619	                            document = self._correct_core(
620	                                item.entity_type,
621	                                item.entity_id,
622	                                item.correction,
623	                                recorded_at,
624	                            )
625	                        except NotFoundError:
626	                            if target in created_here and target not in seen_creates:
627	                                raise ConflictError(
628	                                    f"entity {item.entity_type}/{item.entity_id} is "
629	                                    "corrected before it is created"
630	                                )
631	                            raise
632	                        document["operation"] = "correct"
633	                    else:  # pragma: no cover - parse_batch only yields the two kinds
634	                        raise ValidationError("unknown batch operation")
635	                except TimeVaultError as error:
636	                    message = str(error)
637	                    if not message.startswith("operation "):
638	                        raise type(error)(f"operation {index}: {message}") from error
639	                    raise
640	                results.append(document)
641	            return {"recorded_at": iso(recorded_at), "results": results}

643	        return self._idempotent(key, _batch_operation_name(raw), action, moment)

706	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
707	        start = instant(start, "from")
708	        end = instant(end, "to")
709	        known_at = self.store.now() if known_at is None else instant(known_at, "known_at")
710	        if end <= start:
711	            raise ValidationError("to must be strictly later than from")
712	        if names is not None and len(set(names)) != len(names):
713	            raise ValidationError("attribute may not be repeated")
714	        left = self._projection(entity_type, entity_id, start, known_at)
715	        right = self._projection(entity_type, entity_id, end, known_at)
716	        selected = sorted(set(left) | set(right))
717	        if names is not None:
718	            wanted = set(names)
719	            unknown = sorted(wanted - set(self._all_attributes(entity_type, entity_id)))
720	            if unknown:
721	                raise ValidationError(f"unknown attribute(s): {', '.join(unknown)}")
722	            selected = [name for name in selected if name in wanted]
723	
724	        changes = []
725	        for name in selected:
726	            before = left.get(name)
727	            after = right.get(name)
728	            if before is None and after is None:
729	                continue
730	            if before is not None and after is not None and value_same(before[0], after[0]):
731	                # The value carried across the boundary; only the version that
732	                # supplies it changed, which is not a business-time difference.
733	                continue
734	            if before is None:
735	                kind = "added"
736	            elif after is None:
737	                kind = "removed"
738	            else:
739	                kind = "changed"
740	            changes.append(
741	                {
742	                    "attribute": name,
743	                    "change": kind,
744	                    "before": _value_document(before),
745	                    "after": _value_document(after),
746	                }
747	            )
748	        return {
749	            "type": entity_type,
750	            "id": entity_id,
751	            "from": iso(start),
752	            "to": iso(end),
753	            "known_at": iso(known_at),
754	            "changes": changes,
755	        }

757	    def timeline(
758	        self,
759	        entity_type: str,
760	        entity_id: str,
761	        start: Any,
762	        end: Any,
763	        known_at: Any = None,
764	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
765	        """Walk every state one entity held across a valid-time interval.
766	
767	        The interval ``[from, to)`` is cut into the maximal half-open segments
768	        during which the same set of versions supplies the projection: every
769	        instant inside one segment reads the same attributes from the same
770	        versions.  A boundary lands wherever any visible attribute starts,
771	        ends, is corrected, or is withdrawn — a correction that restates the
772	        same scalar value still splits the interval, because the version
773	        supplying the value changes — while several attributes changing at
774	        one instant share a single boundary.  Segment bounds are clipped to
775	        the query interval, segments never overlap, and a stretch where no
776	        attribute is in effect at all is a gap: it produces no entry.
777	
778	        Everything is interpreted under one ``known_at`` (the current instant
779	        unless given): a correction recorded after it, and any window trim
780	        that correction carried, does not exist for this walk, so repeating
781	        the query over the same committed data always yields the same
782	        document.  The query is read-only: it appends no versions, records no
783	        truncations, and moves no transaction time.
784	        """
785	        start = instant(start, "from")
786	        end = instant(end, "to")
787	        known_at = self.store.now() if known_at is None else instant(known_at, "known_at")
788	        if end <= start:
789	            raise ValidationError("to must be strictly later than from")
790	        # One lock acquisition spans the whole walk, so every window is read
791	        # against the same committed ledger even if a write lands concurrently.
792	        with self.store.lock:
793	            row = self.store.entity_row(entity_type, entity_id)
794	            if row is None:
795	                raise NotFoundError(f"entity {entity_type}/{entity_id} does not exist")
796	            if int(row["created_at"]) > known_at:
797	                raise NotFoundError(
798	                    f"entity {entity_type}/{entity_id} was not recorded yet at that transaction time"
799	                )
800	            grouped = self._grouped_versions(entity_type, entity_id)
801	            windows = {
802	                name: known_windows(versions, known_at) for name, versions in grouped.items()
803	            }
804	
805	        # Every window edge strictly inside the interval is a cut candidate;
806	        # between two neighbouring cuts no window starts or ends, so the
807	        # projection sampled at a segment's start holds for the whole segment.
808	        boundaries: set[int] = set()
809	        for tokens in windows.values():
810	            for _, token_start, token_end in tokens:
811	                if start < token_start < end:
812	                    boundaries.add(token_start)
813	                if token_end is not None and start < token_end < end:
814	                    boundaries.add(token_end)
815	        points = [start, *sorted(boundaries), end]
816	
817	        spans: list[list[Any]] = []
818	        for index in range(len(points) - 1):
819	            seg_start, seg_end = points[index], points[index + 1]
820	            projection: Projection = {}
821	            for name in sorted(windows):
822	                token = project(windows[name], seg_start)
823	                if token is None:
824	                    continue
825	                version, window_start, window_end = token
826	                projection[name] = (
827	                    version.value,
828	                    version.version,
829	                    version.operation,
830	                    window_start,
831	                    window_end,
832	                    version.recorded_at,
833	                )
834	            if not projection:
835	                # Nothing in effect here: a gap, not a segment.
836	                continue
837	            if spans and spans[-1][1] == seg_start and spans[-1][2] == projection:
838	                # A window edge nothing observable hinged on (a version no
839	                # reader can ever select, for instance): the same versions
840	                # keep supplying the projection, so the segment runs on.
841	                spans[-1][1] = seg_end
842	            else:
843	                spans.append([seg_start, seg_end, projection])
844	
845	        return {
846	            "type": entity_type,
847	            "id": entity_id,
848	            "from": iso(start),
849	            "to": iso(end),
850	            "known_at": iso(known_at),
851	            "segments": [
852	                {
853	                    "valid_from": iso(seg_start),
854	                    "valid_end": iso(seg_end),
855	                    "attributes": self._projection_attributes(projection),
856	                }
857	                for seg_start, seg_end, projection in spans
858	            ],
859	        }

861	    def snapshot_diff(
862	        self,
863	        entity_type: str | None = None,
864	        entity_id: str | None = None,
865	        first_as_of: Any = None,
866	        first_known_at: Any = None,
867	        second_as_of: Any = None,
868	        second_known_at: Any = None,
869	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
870	        """Compare the records a scope shows at two bitemporal facets.
871	
872	        Each facet is one ``(as_of, known_at)`` pair, evaluated under exactly
873	        the visibility rules of :meth:`entity_as_of`: a correction recorded
874	        after a facet's ``known_at`` — and any trim it carried — does not
875	        exist for that facet.  Every coordinate defaults to the current
876	        instant and accepts the same forms as the single-entity read.
877	
878	        The scope is the entity or collection the caller limits the
879	        comparison to: a ``type`` and ``id`` name one entity, a ``type``
880	        alone names every entity of that type, and no scope at all spans the
881	        whole store.  Entities are partitioned into ``added`` (visible only
882	        at the second facet), ``removed`` (visible only at the first), and
883	        ``changed`` (visible at both but with different public data content);
884	        an entity whose record is the same at both facets is not part of the
885	        result.  Content is what a read reports as data — attribute values
886	        and their valid windows — so a difference only in the version number
887	        that supplies a value or in the transaction instant it was recorded
888	        at is not a change.  Each category is ordered by the stable
889	        ``(type, id)`` identifier, so repeating the query over the same data
890	        always yields the same document, and an empty store, an empty scope,
891	        or two identical facets simply yields three empty categories.  The
892	        query is read-only: it appends no versions and moves no transaction
893	        time.
894	        """
895	        moment = self.store.now()
896	        if entity_type is not None:
897	            identifier(entity_type, "entity type")
898	        if entity_id is not None:
899	            if entity_type is None:
900	                raise ValidationError("scoping by id requires a type as well")
901	            identifier(entity_id, "entity id")
902	        first = (
903	            moment if first_as_of is None else instant(first_as_of, "first_as_of"),
904	            moment if first_known_at is None else instant(first_known_at, "first_known_at"),
905	        )
906	        second = (
907	            moment if second_as_of is None else instant(second_as_of, "second_as_of"),
908	            moment if second_known_at is None else instant(second_known_at, "second_known_at"),
909	        )
910	        # Hold the lock across both snapshots so a write cannot commit between
911	        # them: the two facets are always evaluated against one ledger, never
912	        # against two halves of a commit in flight.
913	        with self.store.lock:
914	            before = self._snapshot(entity_type, entity_id, *first)
915	            after = self._snapshot(entity_type, entity_id, *second)
916	        added: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
917	        removed: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
918	        changed: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
919	        for type_name, entity in sorted(set(before) | set(after)):
920	            key = (type_name, entity)
921	            earlier = before.get(key)
922	            later = after.get(key)
923	            if earlier is None:
924	                added.append({"type": type_name, "id": entity, "record": later[1]})
925	            elif later is None:
926	                removed.append({"type": type_name, "id": entity, "record": earlier[1]})
927	            elif not _projection_content_same(earlier[0], later[0]):
928	                changed.append(
929	                    {"type": type_name, "id": entity, "before": earlier[1], "after": later[1]}
930	                )
931	        return {
932	            "first": {"as_of": iso(first[0]), "known_at": iso(first[1])},
933	            "second": {"as_of": iso(second[0]), "known_at": iso(second[1])},
934	            "added": added,
935	            "removed": removed,
936	            "changed": changed,
937	        }

939	    def compare_views(
940	        self,
941	        left: Viewpoint,
942	        right: Viewpoint,
943	        record_ids: Iterable[tuple[str, str]] | None = None,
944	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
945	        """Compare the visible records at two complete bitemporal viewpoints.
946	
947	        Each viewpoint is one :class:`Viewpoint` carrying both an ``as_of``
948	        (valid time) and a ``known_at`` (transaction time); both coordinates
949	        are required and must satisfy the same instant constraints as a
950	        plain read's parameters.  ``record_ids`` optionally narrows the
951	        comparison to an iterable collection of ``(type, id)`` logical
952	        record identifiers; when it is omitted every logical record in the
953	        store is compared.
954	
955	        Each side is evaluated under exactly the visibility rules of a plain
956	        read: only versions in effect at that side's valid time, already
957	        knowable at its transaction time, and not withdrawn then are visible,
958	        so a later correction never leaks into the earlier view.  The result
959	        is one flat, stable list ordered by ``(type, id)``: ``added`` entries
960	        are visible only on the right, ``removed`` only on the left, and
961	        ``changed`` entries are visible on both but differ in business value
962	        or in any public version metadata.  Entries whose content and
963	        observable version metadata are identical on both sides are omitted;
964	        the missing side of an addition or removal is reported as ``null``.
965	        Repeated identifiers are compared once, and identifiers that name no
966	        record produce nothing.
967	
968	        Both sides are read inside one acquisition of the store lock, so they
969	        always observe the same committed state — a write that commits
970	        concurrently cannot land between the two reads.  The comparison is
971	        strictly read-only and never mutates the caller's identifier
972	        collection.
973	        """
974	        left_coords = _viewpoint_coordinates(left, "left")
975	        right_coords = _viewpoint_coordinates(right, "right")
976	        wanted = _record_identifiers(record_ids)
977	
978	        with self.store.lock:
979	            # One lock acquisition spans both viewpoints: every other writer
980	            # takes this same lock across its whole transaction, so the two
981	            # sides can never straddle a commit boundary.
982	            if wanted is None:
983	                keys = [(type_name, entity) for type_name, entity, _ in self.store.entity_keys()]
984	            else:
985	                keys = wanted
986	            before: dict[tuple[str, str], tuple[Projection, dict[str, Any]]] = {}
987	            after: dict[tuple[str, str], tuple[Projection, dict[str, Any]]] = {}
988	            for type_name, entity in keys:
989	                left_record = self._visible_record(type_name, entity, *left_coords)
990	                if left_record is not None:
991	                    before[(type_name, entity)] = left_record
992	                right_record = self._visible_record(type_name, entity, *right_coords)
993	                if right_record is not None:
994	                    after[(type_name, entity)] = right_record
995	
996	        differences: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
997	        for key in sorted(set(before) | set(after)):
998	            type_name, entity = key
999	            earlier = before.get(key)
1000	            later = after.get(key)
1001	            if earlier is None:
1002	                kind = DIFF_ADDED
1003	                left_document: dict[str, Any] | None = None
1004	                right_document = later[1]  # type: ignore[union-attr]
1005	            elif later is None:
1006	                kind = DIFF_REMOVED
1007	                left_document = earlier[1]
1008	                right_document = None
1009	            elif not _projection_record_same(earlier[0], later[0]):
1010	                kind = DIFF_CHANGED
1011	                left_document = earlier[1]
1012	                right_document = later[1]
1013	            else:
1014	                # The same observable record on both sides: no difference.
1015	                continue
1016	            differences.append(
1017	                {
1018	                    "type": type_name,
1019	                    "id": entity,
1020	                    "difference": kind,
1021	                    "left": left_document,
1022	                    "right": right_document,
1023	                }
1024	            )
1025	        return {
1026	            "left": {"as_of": iso(left_coords[0]), "known_at": iso(left_coords[1])},
1027	            "right": {"as_of": iso(right_coords[0]), "known_at": iso(right_coords[1])},
1028	            "differences": differences,
1029	        }

1031	    def audit(
1032	        self,
1033	        *,
1034	        entity_type: Any = None,
1035	        entity_id: Any = None,
1036	        attribute: Any = None,
1037	        action: Any = None,
1038	        recorded_from: Any = None,
1039	        recorded_to: Any = None,
1040	        limit: Any = None,
1041	        cursor: Any = None,
1042	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
1043	        """Trace committed ledger changes back to their sources.
1044	
1045	        Every committed version append and every window truncation is one
1046	        immutable audit item.  The query is read-only: it appends nothing and
1047	        moves no transaction time.  Items are ordered by ``recorded_at``
1048	        ascending, and the event id breaks ties inside one millisecond with a
1049	        value that is stable and never reused, so the order is identical after
1050	        a restart.
1051	
1052	        The first response pins the result set: its cursor carries the
1053	        filters and the sequence upper bound assigned at that moment, so
1054	        later concurrent writes never enter later pages and pagination
1055	        neither repeats nor skips an item.  A request carrying a cursor may
1056	        not repeat any filter apart from ``limit``.
1057	        """
1058	        if cursor is not None:
1059	            if not isinstance(cursor, str) or not cursor:
1060	                raise ValidationError("cursor is unknown or malformed")
1061	            pinned_filters, upper_seq, after = _decode_cursor(cursor)
1062	            # With a cursor every filter but limit is fixed by the first page.
1063	            repeated = {
1064	                "type": entity_type,
1065	                "id": entity_id,
1066	                "attribute": attribute,
1067	                "action": action,
1068	                "recorded_from": recorded_from,
1069	                "recorded_to": recorded_to,
1070	            }
1071	            given = sorted(name for name, value in repeated.items() if value is not None)
1072	            if given:
1073	                raise ValidationError(
1074	                    f"filter parameter(s) {', '.join(given)} cannot be combined with cursor"
1075	                )
1076	            filters = pinned_filters
1077	        else:
1078	            filters = self._parse_audit_filters(
1079	                entity_type, entity_id, attribute, action, recorded_from, recorded_to
1080	            )
1081	            after = None
1082	            # Pin the result set to what has committed so far.  A commit that
1083	            # lands after this reading but before the page is read gets a
1084	            # higher sequence and is excluded by the page's ``seq <= upper``
1085	            # bound, so the two reads need not share one lock acquisition.
1086	            upper_seq = self.store.max_audit_seq()
1087	
1088	        page_limit = self._parse_audit_limit(limit)
1089	        if after is not None and not self.store.audit_key_exists(after[0], after[1], upper_seq):
1090	            # The token's position does not exist in this ledger (it was
1091	            # minted against another database), so treat it as unknown.
1092	            raise ValidationError("cursor is unknown or malformed")
1093	        rows = self.store.audit_page(
1094	            after_recorded_at=None if after is None else after[0],
1095	            after_event_id=None if after is None else after[1],
1096	            upper_seq=upper_seq,
1097	            limit=page_limit,
1098	            action=filters.action,
1099	            entity_type=filters.entity_type,
1100	            entity_id=filters.entity_id,
1101	            attribute=filters.attribute,
1102	            recorded_from=filters.recorded_from,
1103	            recorded_to=filters.recorded_to,
1104	        )
1105	        has_more = len(rows) > page_limit
1106	        page = rows[:page_limit]
1107	        items = [self._audit_item(row) for row in page]
1108	        next_cursor: str | None = None
1109	        if has_more and page:
1110	            last = page[-1]
1111	            next_cursor = _encode_cursor(
1112	                filters, upper_seq, (int(last["recorded_at"]), str(last["event_id"]))
1113	            )
1114	        return {"items": items, "next_cursor": next_cursor}

1116	    @staticmethod
1117	    def _parse_audit_limit(raw: Any) -> int:
1118	        if raw is None:
1119	            return DEFAULT_AUDIT_LIMIT
1120	        if isinstance(raw, bool) or isinstance(raw, float):
1121	            raise ValidationError("limit must be an integer between 1 and 500")
1122	        if isinstance(raw, int):
1123	            value = raw
1124	        else:
1125	            try:
1126	                text = str(raw).strip()
1127	                value = int(text)
1128	            except (TypeError, ValueError):
1129	                raise ValidationError("limit must be an integer between 1 and 500") from None
1130	            else:
1131	                if str(value) != text:
1132	                    raise ValidationError("limit must be an integer between 1 and 500")
1133	        if value < 1 or value > MAX_AUDIT_LIMIT:
1134	            raise ValidationError("limit must be between 1 and 500")
1135	        return value

1137	    def _parse_audit_filters(
1138	        self,
1139	        entity_type: Any,
1140	        entity_id: Any,
1141	        attribute: Any,
1142	        action: Any,
1143	        recorded_from: Any,
1144	        recorded_to: Any,
1145	    ) -> AuditFilters:
1146	        if entity_id is not None and entity_type is None:
1147	            raise ValidationError("scoping by id requires a type as well")
1148	        if entity_type is not None:
1149	            entity_type = identifier(entity_type, "entity type")
1150	        if entity_id is not None:
1151	            entity_id = identifier(entity_id, "entity id")
1152	        if attribute is not None:
1153	            attribute = attribute_name(attribute)
1154	        if action is not None:
1155	            if action not in _AUDIT_ACTIONS:
1156	                raise ValidationError(
1157	                    "action must be version_appended or window_truncated"
1158	                )
1159	        start = None if recorded_from is None else instant(recorded_from, "recorded_from")
1160	        end = None if recorded_to is None else instant(recorded_to, "recorded_to")
1161	        if start is not None and end is not None and start >= end:
1162	            raise ValidationError("recorded_from must be strictly earlier than recorded_to")
1163	        return AuditFilters(
1164	            action=action,
1165	            entity_type=entity_type,
1166	            entity_id=entity_id,
1167	            attribute=attribute,
1168	            recorded_from=start,
1169	            recorded_to=end,
1170	        )

1172	    @staticmethod
1173	    def _audit_item(row: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
1174	        """Render one committed ledger event as its public audit document.
1175	
1176	        The fields describing the value at commit time are read off the audit
1177	        row itself, never off the version's current state, so a correction that
1178	        later trims the window cannot rewrite an earlier audit item: the
1179	        append reports the declared end it committed with, and the truncation
1180	        reports the bound learned at its own transaction instant.
1181	        """
1182	        recorded_at = int(row["recorded_at"])
1183	        item: dict[str, Any] = {
1184	            "event_id": str(row["event_id"]),
1185	            "recorded_at": iso(recorded_at),
1186	            "type": str(row["type"]),
1187	            "id": str(row["id"]),
1188	            "attribute": str(row["attribute"]),
1189	            "version": int(row["version"]),
1190	            "action": str(row["action"]),
1191	        }
1192	        if str(row["action"]) == ACTION_VERSION_APPENDED:
1193	            item["operation"] = str(row["operation"])
1194	            item["value"] = None if row["value"] is None else Store.decode(row["value"])
1195	            item["valid_from"] = iso(int(row["valid_from"]))
1196	            declared = row["declared_end"]
1197	            item["declared_end"] = None if declared is None else iso(int(declared))
1198	        else:
1199	            item["valid_end"] = iso(int(row["valid_end"]))
1200	        return item

1205	        self,
1206	        entity_type: str,
1207	        entity_id: str,
1208	        attributes: tuple[Any, ...],
1209	        valid_from: int,
1210	        recorded_at: int,
1211	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:

1214	            raise ConflictError(f"entity {entity_type}/{entity_id} already exists")
1215	        self.store.insert_entity(entity_type, entity_id, recorded_at)
1216	        for attribute in attributes:
1217	            self.store.insert_version(
1218	                entity_type,
1219	                entity_id,
1220	                attribute.name,
1221	                1,
1222	                "assert",
1223	                attribute.value,
1224	                valid_from,
1225	                None,
1226	                recorded_at,
1227	            )

1229	        document["created_at"] = iso(recorded_at)
1230	        return document

1232	    def _correct_core(
1233	        self,
1234	        entity_type: str,
1235	        entity_id: str,
1236	        correction: Correction,
1237	        recorded_at: int,
1238	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
1239	        """Apply one already-parsed correction at a fixed transaction instant.
1240	
1241	        Raises :class:`NotFoundError` when the entity does not exist yet and
1242	        :class:`ConflictError` when the correction's facts would land before the
1243	        entity was recorded.
1244	        """
1245	        row = self.store.entity_row(entity_type, entity_id)
1246	        if row is None:
1247	            raise NotFoundError(f"entity {entity_type}/{entity_id} does not exist")
1248	        if int(row["created_at"]) > recorded_at:
1249	            raise ConflictError(
1250	                f"cannot state a fact about {entity_type}/{entity_id} before it existed"
